00_icebath_after_lifting:
Ice bath after lifting? Read this first.
In a 12-week study, cold water after training blunted strength and muscle gains compared with active recovery (Roberts et al., 2015).
Our rule: sauna after training, cold at another moment.
Did you know this?
#sumisura #icebath #strengthtraining #recovery #brussels
01_sauna_growth_hormone:
Sauna and growth hormone.
1 hour at 80°C, twice a day, for 7 days: growth hormone rose 16-fold in men. The response faded after day 3 and levels normalise within hours (Leppäluoto et al., 1986).
A real signal. Not a shortcut.
How long are your sauna sessions?
#sumisura #sauna #growthhormone #heat #brussels
02_sauna_blood_plasma:
More blood. In 3 weeks.
Post-exercise sauna raised plasma volume by 7.1% and red cell volume by 3.5% (Scoon et al., 2007).
Health, made Sumisura.
Sauna after training: yes or no?
#sumisura #sauna #endurance #bloodvolume #brussels
03_sauna_mortality:
4–7 saunas a week. 20 years of data.
In 2,315 Finnish men, frequent sauna use was associated with 63% lower sudden cardiac death and 40% lower all-cause mortality vs once a week (Laukkanen et al., 2015). Association, not proof.
How often do you sauna?
#sumisura #sauna #hearthealth #longevity #brussels
04_cycling_plasma_buchheit:
4 saunas. +18% plasma.
Well-trained cyclists added 30 min of sauna at 87°C after training. Plasma volume peaked at +17.8% after four sessions (Stanley, Buchheit et al., 2015).
That's the idea behind Sauna Cycling.
Would you add heat to your training?
#sumisura #saunacycling #heattraining #cycling #brussels
05_cycling_haemoglobin:
Heat builds more red blood cells.
Elite cyclists trained 5 × 50 min a week in heat for 5 weeks: haemoglobin mass +2.6% (suit) and +2.4% (chamber) vs -0.7% in controls (Rønnestad et al., 2022).
Heat as training. Not as a spa.
Ever trained in the heat?
#sumisura #heattraining #hemoglobin #vo2max #brussels
06_cycling_heat_to_cold:
Train in the heat. Get fitter in the cold.
10 days of heat training: VO2max +5% and time-trial power +6%, tested in cool conditions (Lorenzo et al., 2010).
The adaptation travels with you.
Would you train in 40°C?
#sumisura #saunacycling #vo2max #heattraining #brussels
07_ihht_why_hyperoxia:
Low oxygen. High oxygen. Why both?
The hypothesis behind IHHT: replacing normal air with mild hyperoxia may strengthen the adaptive response to the low-oxygen phase (Behrendt et al., 2022). Still being tested.
Had you heard of IHHT?
#sumisura #ihht #hypoxia #oxygen #brussels
08_ihht_glucose_bp:
IHHT, blood sugar and blood pressure.
In older patients with cardiovascular or metabolic disease, IHHT at rest reduced blood glucose and blood pressure (systematic review, Behrendt et al., 2022). Patients, small studies.
We measure before and after.
#sumisura #ihht #bloodpressure #metabolichealth #brussels
09_ihht_honest_limits:
What IHHT does NOT do.
In 17 studies of healthy adults aged 50–75, intermittent hypoxia had only a limited effect on body composition, fitness, cardiovascular and bone health (Timon et al., 2023).
Healthy and can train? Train.
Agree?
#sumisura #ihht #training #science #brussels
10_redlight_atp:
Red light and cellular energy.
Red and near-infrared light is absorbed by mitochondria (cytochrome c oxidase), the chain that makes ATP. In muscle research, it increased gains and lowered inflammation (Ferraresi, Huang & Hamblin, 2016).
A support tool. Training does the work.
Have you tried red light?
#sumisura #redlighttherapy #mitochondria #recovery #brussels
11_redlight_skin:
Red light and your skin.
113 people, twice a week, 30 sessions: higher collagen density, less roughness and better complexion vs controls. 611–650 nm was enough (Wunsch & Matuschka, 2014).
Would you try it for your skin?
#sumisura #redlighttherapy #skin #collagen #brussels
12_redlight_wavelengths:
Which wavelength for what?
611–650 nm: skin. 670 nm: the morning eye studies. 810–850 nm: deeper tissue.
Wavelength, dose and timing. That's the protocol.
Did you know the numbers mattered?
#sumisura #redlighttherapy #nearinfrared #photobiomodulation #brussels

16_vo2max_bike_vs_runners:
Runner? A bike test may undersell you.
Runners reached 14% higher oxygen uptake on the treadmill than on the bike; triathletes' bike VO2max was ~93% of treadmill. The legs often tire before heart and lungs peak.
So we note the device and retest on the same one.
Runner or cyclist?
#sumisura #vo2max #running #testing #brussels
17_vo2max_bed_rest:
3 weeks in bed. 40 years of ageing.
In the Dallas Bed Rest Study, 3 weeks of bed rest at age 20 cost 26% of VO2max. 40 years of life cost 27% (McGavock et al., 2009).
Consistency is the product.
Did this surprise you?
#sumisura #vo2max #longevity #fitness #brussels
18_vo2max_4x4:
4×4 intervals vs long, slow cardio.
Same total work, 8 weeks: 4×4 raised VO2max 7.2%, 15/15 raised it 5.5%; long slow and threshold training gave no significant gain. Stroke volume +~10% (Helgerud et al., 2007).
Volume builds the base. Intensity lifts the ceiling.
Do you do intervals?
#sumisura #vo2max #hiit #4x4 #brussels
19_vo2max_age_decline:
Your VO2max drops faster every decade.
3–6% per decade in your 20s and 30s; more than 20% per decade after 70 (Fleg et al., 2005). At every age, the more active were fitter.
Measure it. Then move it.
Do you know your VO2max?
